s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of immunotherapy
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Oral terbinafine trial yielded no improvement
Biopsy showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

shortlist.label: bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation

shortlist.label: urticaria
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques

shortlist.label: cutaneous pseudolymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic rash with perivascular inflammation and eosinophils

shortlist.label: dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic rash with erythematous plaques and perivascular inflammation

raw.rationale: The presence of erythematous annular plaques without scale, superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy, and the lack of response to antifungal treatment (oral terbinafine) are consistent with bullous pemphigoid, especially in the context of the patient's age and immunotherapy regimen.

rejected.label: urticaria
rejected.why: Urticaria typically presents with wheals that are itchy and transient, not persistent erythematous annular plaques.

rejected.label: eczema
rejected.why: Eczema usually presents with scaly, lichenified plaques, which are not described in this case.

rejected.label: cutaneous pseudolymphoma
rejected.why: Cutaneous pseudolymphoma would likely show different histopathological features, such as atypical lymphocytes, which are not mentioned.

rejected.label: dermatitis
rejected.why: Dermatitis is a broad term and the specific findings in this case, such as the presence of numerous eosinophils and the pattern of inflammation, are more suggestive of bullous pemphigoid.
